verdict.label: duplicate
verdict.why: Both functions independently implement the same side-chat start sequence: fork a side chat from a source thread, wait for the new thread shell to reach the client, check the shell is still available, send the first user message with runtimeMode taken from the shell, and discard the empty fork (onlyIfUnused) on failure. The details are identical, including the titleSeed derivation, interactionMode "default", empty attachments, the "Side chat" title, the same failure fallbacks, and the same interrupted-failure check. A shared helper, e.g. startSideChatThread({source, prompt, forkSideChat, deleteThread, startTurn, waitForShell, readShell, report}), could own this sequence. Callers would keep the variation: the mobile creationSource field and alert UI, the web prompt trimming and optional prompt, the pending guard, and the UI navigation (openLinkedThread vs. right-panel store). Each platform's error-presentation callbacks and ID generators would also stay with the callers. Because the same logic is already duplicated across the two platforms, it can drift, for example in the mobile and web wording of the "did not reach this device/client" message.

source_adjudication.contract: Start hidden side chat, wait and verify replicated shell, discard only unused fork on failed wait/shell/send, send initial user turn using shell runtime mode, and expose only after successful required send.
source_adjudication.existing_shared_owner: threadCommands.ts forkSideChat delegates commands.ts forkSideChat; command only dispatches thread.fork latest_stable with sideChat true. It does not wait, discard or send initial turn. Wait/read helpers own shell lookup and availability only. No shared fork/wait/discard/send owner found in pinned grep of forkSideChat and waitForThreadShell callers.
source_adjudication.independent_frozen_source_conclusion: Plausible narrow orchestration: fork hidden side chat, wait for shell, verify shell, discard only unused fork on wait/missing-shell/send failure, send initial user message with title seed/runtime mode/timestamp, then expose thread. Web optional trimmed prompt, pending guard, web tab navigation and mobile alerts/openLinkedThread remain caller policy.
legitimate_variations: Web optional prompt/trim and pending guard; mobile required prompt and creationSource.
ID allocation, interrupted/error presentation, alerts versus callback, command adapters, and navigation remain caller-owned.
Web can intentionally expose an empty fork without a prompt; helper must preserve that branch.
